result:
Solution 3 is correct: the maximum of |P| is 2^999 − 2^499, which I checked with an upper bound and a matching construction.

**Upper bound.** Split the 2^1000 subsets of S into 2^999 complementary pairs {A, S∖A}. The two sets in a pair are disjoint, so P contains at most one of them.

Call a pair bad if A′ = S∖A, which happens exactly when A is a transversal, meaning it takes exactly one element from each of the 500 reflection pairs {i, 1001−i}. If A were in P, condition 3 would force A′ = S∖A into P, and A ∩ (S∖A) = ∅ would violate condition 2. So no set from a bad pair can be in P.

There are 2^500 transversals, which form 2^499 bad pairs. Hence |P| ≤ 2^999 − 2^499.

**Construction.** Take every subset of size at least 501. Any two of these intersect because 501 + 501 > 1000, and the family is closed under reflection because reflection preserves size.

Now handle the 500-element sets that are not transversals. Two 500-sets are disjoint only if they are complements, and a 500-set always meets a set of size at least 501. So we only need to choose at most one set from each complementary pair, while keeping the choice closed under reflection.

- If A′ ≠ S∖A, take A and A′ together and exclude their complements. The complement of A′ is (S∖A)′, so the reflection orbit of the complements is excluded as a unit, and no complementary pair is chosen twice.
- If A′ = A, then (S∖A)′ = S∖A, so we may take either A or S∖A, since each is closed under reflection.

This picks exactly one set from each non-bad complementary pair of 500-sets, so the bound is attained.

**Checking the other solutions.** Solution 1 adds only the 500-sets containing one fixed pair, which is far fewer than the bound allows. Solution 2 gives 2^999, which exceeds the upper bound 2^999 − 2^499 and so cannot be achieved.

CHOICE: 3
